acids is quite soft due to high percentage of unsaturated l`atty acid content. For this reason, it is not possible to use high percentage of rice bran fatty acids in soap However, if rice bran fatty acids arc partially hydrogenated to reduce the unsaturated fatty acids, they can be used in large proportions in the soap. Partially hydrogenated fatty acids resemble Mowrah fatty acids which are ideal for soap making. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a parti-cular requirement of this standard is complied with: the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ).

Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 29 April 1988, after the draft finalized by the Oils and Oilseeds Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council and the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council.

0.2 Rice bran oil is obtained from rice bran by Hydrogenated rice bran fatty solvent extraction. acid is obtained by splitting, distillation and hydrogenation of rice bran oil or by hydrogenation of distilled fatty acids obtained by splitting of rice bran oil or by hydrogenation of the rice bran oil followed by splitting and distillation. 0.3 Rice bran fatty acids contain 20-25 percent of saturated and 75-80 percent of unsaturated fatty acids. The main unsaturated fatty acids are oleic ( 40-50 percent > and linoleic ( 28-42 pcrcent >. The soap obtained from rice bran fatty

2. REQUIREMENTS
2.1 Description - The material shall be obtained by splitting, distillation and hydrogenation; or splitting, hydrogenation and distillation; or hydrogenation, splitting and distillation of rice bran oil.

2.2 The material shall be free from adulterants, sediment, suspended and other foreign matter and separated water. It shall be clear on melting. 2.3 The material shall also comply with the requirements given in Table I when tested in accordance with the methods referred to in co1 4 and 5 of the table. 3. PACKING
AND MARKING

3.1 Packing - The material shall be supplied in suitable containers as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. The packing in mild steel drums shall be avoided. 3.2 Marking - The containers closed and legibly and indelibly shall be securely
marked with the

NOW - The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and superStandard vised by BIS and operated by the producer. marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers, may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Samples shall be stored in such a manner that the temperature of the material does not vary unduly from the normal temperature.

Draw with an appropriate sampling inssmall portions of the material from trument different parts of the selected containers, the total quantity being sufficient to carry out the tests for all characteristics given in Table I. B-3.2 Mix thoroughly all portions 01 the material drawn from the same container to form an individual sample to represent the container. Equal quantities from the selected containers shall be mixed together to form a composite sample to represent the lot. B-2. SCALE OF SAMPLING B-2.0 Samples to determine conformity of the material to this specification shall be selected in accordance with the procedure given below. B-2.1 Lot - All the containers in a single consignment of the material drawn from a single batch of nianufacturc shall constitute the lot. transferred to thoroughly dried bottles which shall then be sealed air-tight with glass stoppers. These shall be labelled with all the particulars of sampling given in B-1.7. One set of the test samples shall be sent to the purchaser and one to the supplier. B-3.4 Referee Sa.mple - The third set of the test samples, bearing the seals of the purchaser and the supplier, shall constitute the referee sample and shall be used in case of dispute between the Furchaser and the supplier. It shall be kept at a place agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. B-4. NUMBER OF TESTS
